newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TVX trebles Czech Kasperske gold estimates.
newsitem.headline: TVX trebles Czech Kasperske gold estimates.

text.p: Czech gold mining company, TVX Bohemia Dulni a.s., a fully owned subsidiary of Canada's TVX Gold Inc., said it had trebled its estimates of gold reserves in the Kasperske Hory area to three million ounces.

"The current estimates of the geological sources of gold in Kasperske Hory have, with investigations still to be completed, been raised to three million ounces (100 tonnes)," TVX said in a statement on Wednesday.
Gold was fixed at $350.10 an ounce in London on Wednesday.
At a news conference the company also sought to pacify vocal protestors who are campaigning against the project on environmental grounds.

"TVX experts have decided on the basis of comments of local residents, without regard to time or expense, that it is possible to use alternatrive methods (to cynaide) of extracting gold from the ore," the statement said.
The town of Kasperske Hory is in the scenic Sumava mountain range, bordering Austria and Germany, which is a favourite with skiers in the winter and hikers in the summer.

Opponents of the project, which include the local council and many residents, are especially worried about the ecological effects of mining methods and they have succeeded in bringing exploration to a halt.

TVX has an exploration licence from the central government in Prague which is valid until 1999 but failure to agree on rights of access with local landowners has stopped exploration pending a decision by the district authority.
